mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% for three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 2.5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 1% signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 YoY < -1%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE > 4.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 2% month-over-month signals a broad-based contraction in economic activity, which depresses earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both INDPRO and HOUST fall by more than 2% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp month-over-month decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 3% signals a contraction in consumer spending, which reduces corporate revenue and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS < -3% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated fall in both CPIAUCSL (inflation) and FEDFUNDS below 1.5% for two consecutive months signals a deflationary environment with accommodative policy, which boosts risk appetite and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 1.5% AND FEDFUNDS < 1.5% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS are below 1.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) by more than 1% month-over-month for three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS grows by more than 1% MoM for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 2% month-over-month signals a broad-based supply-side expansion, which increases corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both INDPRO and HOUST rise by more than 2% MoM.
